worktree: source: src/ec/nist.rs, src/ec/oct.rs, src/ec/print.rs, src/ec/prn.rs, src/ec/sm2_key.rs, src/ec/smpl2.rs, src/ec/smpl.rs, src/ec/support.rs; ledger: REMAINING-AUDIT.txt, AUDITED-FILES.txt, PERFILE-INDEX.md section 56 and this file.
scope: The eight files named as next by M50. Three audited with no source change. Repairs: the GF2m method table's three default-oct slots are NULL again (D1); two allocator seam file strings gain the admitted build record's __FILE__ prefix (D2/D3); one allocation extent is checked (D4); one unsafe API's NULL precondition is stated instead of describing UB as an expected fault (D5, documentation only). No new production unsafe operation, FFI symbol, allocation extent/line, repr(C) layout, exported signature or unsafe lint attribute.

safety_contract_repairs.note: point_set_compressed_coordinates, point2oct and oct2point are None again, matching ec2_smpl.c:954-956; EC_FLAGS_DEFAULT_OCT already dispatches those operations by field type in ec_oct.c, so no in-crate behaviour changes.
FILE_EC_OCT is now ../../src/openssl-3.6.4/crypto/ec/ec_oct.c, matching the admitted authority's __FILE__ for the CRYPTO_malloc/CRYPTO_free pair at :147/:151.
FILE is now ../../src/openssl-3.6.4/crypto/ec/ecp_smpl.c, matching the admitted authority's __FILE__ for CRYPTO_malloc_array at :1229 and CRYPTO_free at :1357.

EC_POINT_point2hex computes buf_len * 2 + 2 with checked_mul/checked_add; an unrepresentable extent answers NULL (the allocation-failure answer) instead of wrapping to a short allocation and overrunning it.

ossl_ec_curve_nist2nid_int's # Safety now requires a non-NULL name. The previous text called a NULL dereference in strcmp an expected fault; a safe-looking permitted input that is actually UB is not a sound contract.

file_dispositions.note: crypto/ec/ecp_nist.c. Private BN_CTX values are released on refusal and success paths; field_mod_func is only a copied callback pointer; no allocator seam and no secret copy.
crypto/ec/ecp_oct.c and ec_oct.c. M51-D2 seam prefix. Length checks precede every write; point2buf's into_raw is the single transfer edge and the encoder-refusal path frees through Drop.
crypto/ec/ec_print.c. M51-D4 checked extent. The shared err tail releases the octet block over the decoder-written length and clears a point only when this call allocated it.
crypto/ec/eck_prn.c and ec_ameth.c:717-720. off is clamped to 128 before the 133-byte formatter writes; the p/a/b/gen_buf/ctx release order matches the authority's err label.
crypto/sm2/sm2_key.c. Only max = BN_dup(order) is allocated and BN_free'd on every path; the private scalar is borrowed, never copied.

crypto/ec/ec2_smpl.c and ec2_oct.c. M51-D1 restores the authority's NULL default-oct slots. Group/point clear-finish cleanse with BN_clear_free; every temporary lives in a BN_CTX released on all exits.

crypto/ec/ecp_smpl.c. M51-D3 seam prefix. prod_z is one owned CRYPTO_malloc_array block with BN_clear_free elements; field_inv creates a secure BN_CTX when ctx is NULL; the arithmetic and branch order match the authority.
crypto/evp/ec_support.c. M51-D5 states the non-NULL precondition of the strcmp-based lookup; table order and case sensitivity match.

reconciliation.method: The eight audited files were removed from the head of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt and merged into AUDITED-FILES.txt in path order. Counts are entries, not files touched.

retained_observations: print.rs's OwnedClearBuf trusts the decoder-reported oct_buf_len not to exceed the buffer extent passed to OPENSSL_hexstr2buf_ex. The authority has the same precondition and the decoder establishes it; it remains an internal owner precondition, not a new public unsafe API.

The M51-D1 method-table change is not observably behavioural inside the crate because EC_FLAGS_DEFAULT_OCT dispatches by field type; a direct observer of EC_GF2m_simple_method() now sees the authority's NULL slots.

Out of this batch but the same seam-prefix class: src/ec/ecdh_ossl.rs:61 and src/ec/ecdsa_ossl.rs:66 still use short crypto/ec/... FILE constants for their CRYPTO_* calls. They were audited in M49 and are left unchanged; a later ledger pass should decide whether M49's evidence remains valid or needs reissuing.

sm2_key.rs and all eight files hold no private scalar copy: SM2's scalar is borrowed for a range comparison, and the EC scalar/point intermediates remain in mult.rs and ecdsa_ossl.rs, whose cleansing was audited in M49/M50.
